title: Beyond Carbon: Towards a Social Lifecycle Assessment Framework for Green Façades and Green Roofs in Sustainable Building Design: A Systematic Review
content: Green facades and green roofs are increasingly promoted as core strategies for building decarbonisation, energy-efficient design, and ecological building concepts, with their environmental performance extensively documented through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). However, the social dimension of these interventions occupant wellbeing, labour conditions embedded in the production of renewable and recycled materials, equity of access to green retrofits, and community acceptance remains largely absent from mainstream sustainability assessment. This paper conducts a systematic review, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, of the LCA literature on green roofs and living walls published between 2015 and 2025, screening 264 records identified in Scopus and Web of Science down to 45 included studies. The review finds that environmental, economic, and technical performance evaluations dominate this literature, and that the evidence base is heavily concentrated on green roofs (91% of included studies) rather than green facades or living walls (9%). Only one included study applies a full Social Lifecycle Assessment (S-LCA) methodology to a green roof, confirming that social sustainability evaluation of vegetated building envelopes exists but remains an isolated, non-cumulative contribution rather than an established practice. Drawing on the identified findings, this paper develops a preliminary S-LCA framework for green roofs and living walls, modifying the five UNEP/SETAC stakeholder categories to better reflect the specific characteristics and social implications of vegetated envelopes. The framework provides a more comprehensive approach for researchers and policy-makers to assess the broader impacts of building greening strategies beyond conventional environmental performance indicators.
